item.title: os/exec's StdoutPipe Footgun: How cmd.Wait() Ate My Last Frame (Twice)
item.description: shipmates spends most of its life spawning claude (and codex) processes and reading newline-delimited JSON off their stdout. The last frame of a turn is the important one, a result frame with the cost, the model and the final text. Stderr matters too, because that’s where Claude Code tells you Invalid API key · Please run /login. For a while I was throwing both away under load, and the cause is documented right there in the os/exec godoc. I fixed it in one package and then found the exact same bug again a month later in another.

item.title: Stop Running PHP on tokio's spawn_blocking - Own Your Thread Pool
item.description: For most of its life, ePHPm ran every PHP request on tokio’s spawn_blocking pool. It works. It passes tests, it serves benchmarks fine, and it’s the first thing anybody reaches for when they need to call blocking code from async Rust. It’s also quietly wrong for a language runtime, in ways that only show up under overload or after a crash. Over the last three weeks it got replaced with a pool of OS threads that ePHPm owns, first behind a config flag, then as the default, and as of v0.9.0 the spawn_blocking engine is gone.

item.title: Two Small go-proxmox Fixes: A Watch Channel That Never Closed, and WithRetry
item.description:
Two changes from the v0.5 to v0.7 stretch of go-proxmox that are too small for a post each but are worth knowing about if you write long-running tooling against Proxmox. One is a bug in code I wrote about in 2022, the other is a feature that replaces a retry loop everybody was writing for themselves.
